surface: the JSON reader's field text: AnalyzeByJSonPath.getString over json-path 2.9.0, filters and slices
provenance: source-executed on a host JVM; NOT the four-stage device oracle

frozenSources.role: the JSON reader the rule path reaches: getString is the field-text boundary this corpus compares
the rule splitter and {$.rule} inner-rule pass AnalyzeByJSonPath.getString runs before the read

library.wraps: gradle/libs.versions.toml:22, the version the frozen AnalyzeByJSonPath.kt calls

frozenHashCheck: The script runs `sha1sum -c tool/jsonpath_oracle/frozen.sha1` in the frozen checkout before compiling, so a different or dirty checkout cannot emit a golden labelled with the baseline revision.

toolchain.jsonPath: json-path-2.9.0 (with json-smart-2.5.0, accessors-smart-2.5.0, slf4j-api-2.0.11, asm-9.6, verified against tool/jsonpath_probe/jars.sha256)
toolchain.androidxAnnotation: annotation-jvm-1.10.0 (compile classpath only, for the frozen @Keep)

determinism: The harness runs every case twice and refuses the output when the two runs differ. json-path 2.9.0 reads no clock, no random source and no ambient state here, so this is a guard against a future corpus row rather than a known non-deterministic branch.

notCompared.name: declared-scan-index-guard
notCompared.reason: The matrix row names `$..[N]...` as refused by name: the frozen ScanPathToken.walkArray element-index guard is what decides what it answers, and this reader refuses the form instead of guessing it. [docs/compatibility/book-source-capability-matrix.md:121]

notCompared.name: declared-scan-wildcard
notCompared.reason: The same guard reached through the `$..*.` spelling. [docs/compatibility/book-source-capability-matrix.md:121]

notCompared.name: declared-operator-triple-equals
notCompared.reason: The library knows `===` and this reader does not run it, which the matrix row names. [docs/compatibility/book-source-capability-matrix.md:121]

notCompared.name: declared-operator-contains
notCompared.reason: `contains` is one of the operators the matrix row lists as not run. [docs/compatibility/book-source-capability-matrix.md:121]

notCompared.name: declared-function-in-filter-path
notCompared.reason: A function call in a filter path, which the matrix row lists among the refused path forms. [docs/compatibility/book-source-capability-matrix.md:121]

notCompared.name: declared-quoted-property
notCompared.reason: A quoted property name, refused by name in the matrix row. [docs/compatibility/book-source-capability-matrix.md:121]

notCompared.name: declared-slice-step
notCompared.reason: `[::n]` is refused by the library and by this reader, so the compared text the frozen side would carry is the empty one getString leaves — the two shapes differ and the matrix row names both. [docs/compatibility/book-source-capability-matrix.md:121]

notCompared.name: declared-slice-over-map
notCompared.reason: The recorded divergence in the matrix row: a definite slice over a non-array is a named FormatException where the frozen reader swallows the library PathNotFoundException into an empty text. [docs/compatibility/book-source-capability-matrix.md:121]

notCompared.name: declared-slice-over-null
notCompared.reason: The same divergence over a null value. [docs/compatibility/book-source-capability-matrix.md:121]

containerTypes: The class names behind the container rendering, read on the frozen classpath: json-path's default reader answers a matched object as java.util.LinkedHashMap (superclass HashMap) and a matched array as net.minidev.json.JSONArray. The object form is therefore AbstractMap.toString, {k=v, k2=v2} in the document's key order, and only the JSONArray writer escapes.

productFix.found: The first run of this corpus (60 rules, before the rendering rows below were added) compared 58 and failed these two: a rule whose matches are objects or arrays carried Dart's rendering of them ({k: v}, [z, y]) where the frozen field text carries json-smart's ({k=v}, ["z","y"]).
productFix.fixed: lib/source/json_source_rules.dart: _fieldText now renders a match through _matchedText/_mapText/_arrayText/_jsonValueText/_jsonMapText/_scalarText, the frozen toString forms. test/jsonpath_differential_test.dart is the comparison.
productFix.effect: After the fix the two rows compare, the eleven declared rows are reported in notCompared by name above, and the JSONPath row carries a fixture instead of a gap.

reviewRound.found: A fresh-context read of the diff found that _jsonEscape modelled the wrong escaper: it wrote eight shorthands minus the slash, treated only < U+0020 as a control range, and lowercased the hex. The frozen escaper is net.minidev.json.JStylerObj$Escape4Web.escape (json-smart selects Escape4Web for the writer's style, which sets _protect4Web).
reviewRound.before: For the new row's document the old model wrote slash=[a/b] raw, left U+0085, U+007F and the U+201C/U+2014/U+2026 band raw, and wrote the escaped controls as \u000b and \u001f (lowercase, a two-nibble tail).
reviewRound.after: The golden's own text for render-escaper-classes is {slash=["a\/b"], control=["p\u000Bq","x\u0085y","d\u007Fe","e\u001Ff"], wide=["\u201C中\u201D\u2014\u2026"], quoted=["a\"b","c\\d"], inArray=[{"a\/b":"c\/d"}]} — the slash escaped, the three ranges as four uppercase hex digits, and the object form's own string values still raw.
reviewRound.corpus: One render row was added (render-escaper-classes, 85 rules now), the array-element filter row was corrected to the probe's own rule (it had a leaf key appended that made it an empty row, and the transcript line for it is `$.tags[?(@ =~ /y/)] ok List[List[String(y)]]`), three corpus notes were rewritten to the answers their own row pins (filter-regex-empty-value, filter-exists-null-value / filter-truthiness-null-value and filter-bare-boolean-field), four more that asserted a wrong mechanism or count were corrected (filter-eq-number-matches-string-one, filter-gt-string-field, filter-ne-number, filter-regex-ungrouped-alternation), and plain-slice was renamed plain-negative-index.
reviewRound.guards: test/jsonpath_differential_test.dart now checks this manifest against the corpus and the golden (names, rules, kinds, reasons, frozenText/frozenRead, the compared count), matches a declared row's refusal type against its kind, and writes the notCompared list to stdout so a green run still reports it.

deviceRow.reason: The four-stage device oracle entry that would run a JSON rule inside the frozen APK process does not exist. This host harness executes the frozen AnalyzeByJSonPath.kt and RuleAnalyzer.kt bytes against the same library release and is not a device golden.

outOfCorpus: a number at or above 1e7 or below 1e-3: the JVM writes scientific notation where Dart writes a decimal, and no row here reaches that band
the failure shapes of the declared rows themselves: only the refused text is frozen, and the contract does not compare exception classes
the rule-level &&/||/%% merges over more than one branch and the {{...}} template form: those are the adapter's source-derived rows, not this corpus's boundary

the sibling list boundary, named and reachability-stated: the frozen AnalyzeByJSonPath.getStringList renders each matched element through toString() too (AnalyzeByJSonPath.kt:83-86, reached from AnalyzeRule.getStringList for a JSON rule at AnalyzeRule.kt:204), while the product's _pageTexts (lib/source/json_source_pipeline.dart, the nextContentUrl/nextTocUrl page walk) reads JsonSourceRules.list and stringifies each item with Dart's '$item', so a container item carries Dart's {k: v}/[a, b] where the frozen carries {k=v}/the quoted array form. Nothing reaches it: the only product entries are ruleToc.nextTocUrl and ruleContent.nextContentUrl, none of the operator's 150 used sources declares either on a JSON-pipeline source, and across the 2026-09-17 export (676 JSON-pipeline records, 93 declared next-page rules) no rule ends in an index/wildcard/slice/filter token (58 script-only, 31 a literal template, 4 a path ending in a property name). The element-list entry keeps raw matches (the frozen getList), not this boundary; ticket #78's list lane left the container rendering named rather than routing it under an unproven model
